description:
A closure built by a helper and selected by a case fails on its second use: the interpreter prints the first dbg and then stops with "backend value was absent and cannot be materialized" in a continuation delivery into main/0 (entry 10), from FunctionId 38's tail. Same failure at base 5ea6a5830 (top of stack #258) and with fz-xxd.10 revision 3, so it predates that work. Found while shrinking closure_capture_requirement_projection.

Reproduce: fz2 interp q2.fz (prints 3, then fails). Expected: 3 then 3 (both reductions multiply 1*1*3).

    def mailbox(x, acc), do: x * acc
    def wrap(reducer), do: fn (x, acc) -> reducer.(x, acc) end
    def select(choose, reducer) do
      case choose do
        true -> wrap(&mailbox/2)
        _ -> wrap(reducer)
      end
    end
    
    def main() do
      send(self(), fn (x, acc) -> x * acc end)
      reducer = receive do f -> f end
      dbg(Enum.reduce([1, 3], 1, wrap(reducer)))
      send(self(), true)
      choose = receive do value -> value end
      dbg(Enum.reduce([1, 3], 1, select(choose, reducer)))
    end

Differs from the passing p1 shape only in that the first reduce passes wrap(reducer) (not a literal lambda), the list is [1, 3], and both results go to dbg.
Paper first: shrink further, answer by hand which executable should deliver the value, find the first difference. Check JIT and AOT too (three-path parity).

No longer reproduces (2026-10-23): q2.fz prints 3 then 3 on interp at fz-sc8/distill-fz 2446c9cb0. Closed as not reproducing; reopen with a fresh repro if the symptom returns.
title: A helper-built closure chosen by a case loses its value on the second reduce
